new_destinations.name: Geelong
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a "Geelong" city page whose See list names these places; Victoria's second city and regional hub.

new_destinations.name: Bellarine Peninsula
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage "Queenscliff" page describes the Bellarine Peninsula town; Bellarine Peninsula is the tourism brand (Visit Geelong and the Bellarine).

new_destinations.name: Surf Coast
new_destinations.name_evidence: Tourism brand "Surf Coast" (Surf Coast visitor region at the start of the Great Ocean Road); Wikivoyage Great Ocean Road and Torquay (Victoria) pages list these stops. Name to be confirmed against a visitor source in Pipeline C.

new_destinations.name: Lorne
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a "Lorne" page; a major Great Ocean Road summer town.

new_destinations.name: Apollo Bay
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage has an "Apollo Bay" page that lists the Otway walks and falls; Great Ocean Road mid-point town and base for the Otways and Cape Otway.

new_destinations.name: Port Campbell National Park
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage has "Port Campbell National Park" and "Port Campbell" pages; Twelve Apostles is the headline attraction of the Great Ocean Road.

new_destinations.name: Warrnambool
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a "Warrnambool" page; coastal city and base on the Shipwreck Coast.

new_destinations.name: Portland
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a "Portland (Victoria)" page; Victoria's first permanent European settlement.

stronger_left_out.name: Camperdown
stronger_left_out.reason: A town whose only listed draw on Wikivoyage is Mt Leura and the lakes view, which are the attractions; a town is not a spot beside its own attractions (COVERAGE: town wrapper).

stronger_left_out.name: Wye River
stronger_left_out.reason: Village with koalas duplicating Kennett River; no distinct draw (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Aireys Inlet
stronger_left_out.reason: Village is a wrapper for Split Point Lighthouse; keep the attraction (COVERAGE town wrapper rule).

stronger_left_out.name: Cape Otway
stronger_left_out.reason: Duplicate of Cape Otway Lightstation, already a candidate (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Rip View Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Part of Point Lonsdale headland walks (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Lady Julia Percy Island
stronger_left_out.reason: Reached only by charter, no regular landing (rule 2).

stronger_left_out.name: Peterborough, Victoria
stronger_left_out.reason: Small town; draw is the nearby Bay of Islands (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Point Impossible Beach
stronger_left_out.reason: Lesser beach near Torquay, clothes-optional designation only; no distinct visitor draw (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Lake Colac
stronger_left_out.reason: For: Wikivoyage Colac names the largest freshwater lake in Victoria, birdwatching, botanic gardens beside it. Against: one source, shallow drought-hit lake, plain town lakeshore.

stronger_left_out.name: Lavers Hill
stronger_left_out.reason: Gateway village, not a draw itself (candidate note; rule 2).

stronger_left_out.name: Geelong Library and Heritage Centre
stronger_left_out.reason: a civic building seen from the pavement

stronger_left_out.name: East Beach, Port Fairy
stronger_left_out.reason: For: tourism board names it for whale watching, main town beach. Against: one source, overlaps Port Fairy's coast and Griffiths Island, no distinct activity beyond seasonal whales.

strongest_outsiders.name: Port Fairy
strongest_outsiders.note: Port Fairy centre is ~28 km west of Warrnambool, an independent base (own Wikivoyage city page) that visitors reach on its own; outside Warrnambool's span (centre-to-centre 28 km vs 17 km reach) and with only three kept places it does not make a destination.

strongest_outsiders.name: Budj Bim Cultural Landscape
strongest_outsiders.note: ~43 km from Portland and ~60 km from Warrnambool, outside both spans; reached via Heywood/Macarthur on its own.

strongest_outsiders.name: Mount Leura
strongest_outsiders.note: ~44 km from Port Campbell National Park centre and ~55 km from Warrnambool; reached from Camperdown on the volcanic plains, outside both spans.

strongest_outsiders.name: The Crags
strongest_outsiders.note: About 10 km from Port Fairy on its own coast, ~35 km from Warrnambool: standalone with Port Fairy.

strongest_outsiders.name: Griffiths Island Lighthouse
strongest_outsiders.note: Part of the Port Fairy cluster, ~28 km from Warrnambool: standalone with Port Fairy.

strongest_outsiders.name: Mount Eccles National Park
strongest_outsiders.note: ~45 km from Portland and outside its span; Budj Bim and Mount Eccles are two kept places only (a national park with fewer than four spots is standalone, never a spot of another park).

benchmark: Region-specific: Ninety Mile Beach etc. are other regions. Benchmark-relevant items here: Twelve Apostles placed (highest views 83872, 3 sources); no vehicle/operator spots kept (Otway Fly is a place; Bellarine Peninsula Railway kept with named journey rationale); negative benchmarks (library civic building, local parks/gardens, lookouts inside larger spots) rejected; gateway villages (Lavers Hill, Peterborough, Camperdown) rejected as town wrappers/gateways.
